title: Robust Mahalanobis Applications : Surveillance anomaly detection
description: Online Robust Mahalanobis is a statistical method for anomaly detection in robotic joint residuals. It measures how far a new sample deviates from a healthy baseline distribution using a robust Mahalanobis distance metric that is resistant to outliers. The method updates estimates of location and scatter online using averaged stochastic gradient descent, enabling real-time anomaly scoring. It is designed to detect faults such as payload changes in robotic arms by flagging samples that fall outside a learned healthy range. The approach improves on classical Mahalanobis distance by using robust estimators (geometric median and median covariation matrix) to avoid masking effects caused by outliers. This technique is presented as a research and utility module rather than a vulnerability or active threat.

aiSummary: The Online Robust Mahalanobis method computes anomaly scores by measuring the Mahalanobis distance of new samples from a healthy joint residual distribution, using robust estimators for location (geometric median) and scatter (median covariation matrix). These estimators have a 50% breakdown point, meaning they resist corruption from up to half the samples. The method updates estimates online via averaged stochastic gradient descent, allowing real-time adaptation to new data. The anomaly score is the Mahalanobis distance calculated without matrix inversion, using eigendecomposition of the median covariation matrix. This approach mitigates the masking effect seen in classical estimators that use sample mean and covariance, which are sensitive to outliers. The method has been demonstrated on synthetic robotic arm data to detect payload faults and drift anomalies with high accuracy and low false alarm rates. It is a statistical anomaly detection technique rather than a security vulnerability or exploit.
aiImpact: This content describes a statistical anomaly detection technique for robotic systems and does not represent a security vulnerability or threat. There is no direct impact on software security or system integrity. The method aims to improve fault detection in robotics by robustly identifying anomalous sensor readings. No exploitation or malicious activity is associated with this technique.
